In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in the cuprates the ARPES spectra contain the contributions from the bipolarons, delocalized electrons, and autolocalized electrons.
in the electron-phonon system with SBTS the carrier distribution is determined by the phonon field and is not a function of the carrier momentum.
the spontaneous breaking of the translation symmetry is a key factor in explaining all the peculiarities of ARPES and optical spectra of cuprates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the SBTS is the main reason for the broad bands and waterfalls in the ARPES spectra of the cuprates and the distribution function of charge carriers with spontaneously broken translations symmetry is the main tool to study such systems.

we have shown that the spontaneous breaking of the electron and phonon translational symmetry in cuprates leads to the partition of the momentum distribution of the carriers into two parts: one part of the momentum distribution corresponds to the autolocalized carriers and the other one to the delocalized ones.
in systems with strong coupling between electrons and phonons the electron-phonon correlation is a key to the understanding of many phenomena observed in such systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the carrier distribution function in electron-phonons systems with spontaneously broken translation symmetry and vertical dispersion in ARPES spectra can be used to study both the temperature and doping evolution of the carrier distribution function and the ARPES spectra of the system.
spontaneous translational symmetry breaking in the electron-phonon system with `vertical dispersion` in ARPES spectra is a universal property of the cuprates and other materials.
in systems with SBTS the momentum distribution of the charge carrier is no longer sharp and the carrier concentration is a function of its momentum.
